races.name: Dandara Golwg Gwendraeth Handicap

runners_data.name: Outer Edge
runners_data.note: Modest recent form (4844-5) but has course and distance experience; natural hold-up horse whose preferred rear-positioned style is unavailable in this small field, forcing her to race closer than ideal — Gina Mangan will need to make a decision early about whether to push forward or accept a wide, exposed passage.|

runners_data.name: Beelzebub
runners_data.note: Won last time out over this exact 6f trip on good ground 7 days ago, giving Tony Carroll's string a live chance on the formbook; though a genuine closer by trade, the recent winning form is the headline here, and Myla Coppins' 7lb claim softens the weight burden — the tight field means he won't get the strong pace he ideally wants.|

runners_data.name: In Denial
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with only two runs on good ground and a modest record (10th, 3rd) in similar conditions; holds up naturally but has done so over this trip before, and Billy Loughnane's experience at this level is a plus — the 34-day break and trainer's blank 14-day strike rate temper enthusiasm.|

runners_data.name: Tickettothestars
runners_data.note: The best record on good ground of any horse in the race (9 runs, 1W 2P) and ran second at this level over 6f on good just 24 days ago; Rod Millman's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up performer with strong similar-going form, and Darragh Keenan's familiarity with the style makes this a consistent each-way threat.|

runners_data.name: Lieutenant Sir
runners_data.note: Archie Watson three-year-old with a single placing on good ground from four attempts; a natural hold-up type pushed into a midfield slot by the congested field, and Luke Morris will likely find the six-runner, leader-dominated shape restricts his usual late challenge — limited scope for the style to function as intended.|

runners_data.name: Jackie Brown
runners_data.note: The only front-runner in the race and therefore structurally pivotal; David Egan for Adrian Wintle, whose 14-day record reads 5/14, is an active booking — headgear noted (hg:p), and while Jackie Brown lacks a win in recent form, the uncontested lead on good turf over 6f at Ffos Las places her in a uniquely advantageous tactical position relative to all rivals.|

races.paceDynamic: Jackie Brown is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge her early, David Egan can control tempo from the front at whatever clip suits — this sets up as a genuinely uncontested lead, which on good turf over 6f at Ffos Las is a significant structural advantage. The five hold-up types behind her — Outer Edge, Beelzebub, Lieutenant Sir, In Denial, and Tickettothestars — will be chasing throughout, and with a six-runner field the chance of a bunched, slowly-run affair that plays into closers' hands is real but secondary. This field carries more true hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Outer Edge, Beelzebub, and Lieutenant Sir are all redistributed to the midfield map position, but they are genuine closers by nature and will likely be strung out behind the leader rather than racing prominently. The race shape strongly favours a front-runner who can dictate a moderate, uncontested gallop and quicken clear — Jackie Brown's profile is structurally dominant, and hold-up runners face the classic problem of having too much ground to make up in a small field where the leader is never truly pressured.

watchPoints.text: Jackie Brown's early sections are the key to the race — if Egan sets a truly honest gallop rather than a dawdle, the hold-up horses will have more chance of closing; watch the first furlong split closely.

Beelzebub's recent win came just 7 days ago — monitor market moves as a sharp reappearance on identical going and trip could mean Carroll is confident, but the compressed turnaround and style mismatch in a slowly-run race are real risks.

Tickettothestars has the strongest similar-going profile in the field (9 runs, 1W 2P on good) and ran second recently — if the pace is honest, this horse's closing ability over 6f on good ground makes it the most dangerous pursuer of Jackie Brown.

With five hold-up horses behind a single front-runner in a 6-runner field, watch for a clustering effect on the home turn where several closers make simultaneous moves — positional awareness from jockeys like Luke Morris and Billy Loughnane could be decisive in a tight finish.

The going report confirms Good across the board at Ffos Las today — no bias flagged, but horses with proven good-ground form (Tickettothestars, Beelzebub) hold a meaningful edge over those with predominantly standard/artificial surface histories (Outer Edge, Lieutenant Sir).

races.name: Diplomat Hotel Handicap

runners_data.name: Rogue Enforcer
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Archie Watson (2/32 in 14 days, modest yard form), wearing a hood, returning 23 days off — zero wins and zero places in 4 comparable similar-going runs this season, making it hard to fancy him unless the pace fully collapses.

runners_data.name: All Ways Glamorous
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner ridden by conditional Gina Mangan for a low-volume trainer (0/3 in 14 days); 42 days since last run is the slight fitness query, but two wins and six places from 8 comparable Good-ground efforts give her a strong pace-fit profile — style advantage is substantial here.

runners_data.name: El Bufalo
runners_data.note: David Egan takes the mount for Thomas Faulkner (2/7 in 14 days, decent short-term form); holds a hold-up profile with tongue-tie added, but only 3 places from 15 similar-going runs and no wins in that sample — dependent on a pace collapse that looks unlikely.

runners_data.name: Zighy
runners_data.note: George Boughey's 3-year-old arrives in excellent yard form (7/27 in 14 days) with Billy Loughnane aboard; naturally prominent, should press All Ways Glamorous closely enough to be dangerous if the leader weakens, and his two recent course wins (both on Standard) show he handles sharp tracks.

runners_data.name: Comic Strip
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer — Simon & Ed Crisford's 3-year-old has won over 5f and placed twice — but displaced to midfield on the pace map because both Zighy and All Ways Glamorous will edge him for early position; Sean D Bowen will need him to produce more than his recent form (1/9 in similar going) suggests he can from a compromised berth.

races.paceDynamic: All Ways Glamorous is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Zighy and Comic Strip as genuine prominent types competing for early position, she faces no serious pressure for the lead on this flat 5f Ffos Las track. Zighy (Billy Loughnane) and Comic Strip are both naturally prominent but cannot all occupy the same berth — Comic Strip is most likely to be shuffled back from its natural slot given Zighy's youth, recent course experience and stronger trainer form (Boughey 7/27 in 14 days). All Ways Glamorous can therefore control fractions at a comfortable, sustainable clip, which on Good ground over a straight 5f shapes up as a thoroughly lead-friendly contest. The field contains more prominent intent than the map can accommodate, and the race shape that emerges — one uncontested front-runner with the rail and the pace — strongly favours hold-up horses only if the leader ties up, which looks unlikely given the lack of a genuine pace duel; the primary tactical beneficiaries are those who can produce a strong late surge from off the pace, but even they face a significant task against a relaxed and untroubled pace-setter.

scenarios.body: If All Ways Glamorous secures a comfortable lead and is allowed to bowl along at her own rhythm without a sustained challenge.

watchPoints.text: All Ways Glamorous jumps cleanly and immediately — if Gina Mangan lets her stride into an uncontested lead, no one in this field has the natural pace to close her down on flat Ffos Las ground.

Monitor Zighy's starting position and early stride — if Billy Loughnane pushes him forward aggressively from the outset, he is the one horse capable of harrying All Ways Glamorous and changing the pace shape entirely.

Comic Strip's actual race position in the early stages will determine everything — if Sean D Bowen cannot push forward past Zighy, Comic Strip is effectively racing from a position that doesn't suit and his chance diminishes sharply.

El Bufalo's tongue-tie is a first-time headgear marker worth noting — if it produces sharper early energy than his hold-up profile suggests, he could complicate the prominent picture, though his similar-going record (0W0P from 15) tempers expectations.

Rogue Enforcer's hood and return from 23 days off for a yard in modest form (2/32 in 14 days) warrants monitoring in the market — any significant support would suggest stable confidence that his flat 5f form figures don't obviously justify.

races.name: Dress For The Occasions Handicap

runners_data.name: Mayberry Moon
runners_data.note: 293 days off the track is the dominant concern for this two-year-old hold-up filly; David Egan gives the partnership quality in the saddle, and she has form on good ground and over 7f, but the long absence and her natural rear-of-field style leave her needing everything to fall perfectly.

runners_data.name: Norfolk Blue
runners_data.note: Wore headgear last time (p) and ran a solid second over 7f on good ground 15 days ago, showing this trip and conditions suit; Taylor Fisher is a conditional claiming rider, and the hold-up style means she will likely be carried further back than ideal, though her recent form is the most current in the field.

runners_data.name: Quick Quasar
runners_data.note: The only confirmed pace-setter in the race and will have the run entirely on her own terms from stall one; her STYLE_FIT flag notes she is racing somewhat out of natural role here, but with no rival to push her, she can dictate completely — her wins at 7f on Tapeta suggest she handles this trip.

runners_data.name: Flyta
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's three-year-old has turf headgear and ran a fine second on good ground over 8f suggesting stamina is not an issue; a genuine hold-up horse placed to midfield on the map because the field is saturated at the rear, meaning Billy Loughnane will face a positional compromise from the outset.

runners_data.name: Strong Voice
runners_data.note: Has placed at 7f on Standard and 7f on Standard before a disappointing run 79 days ago on good ground; James Horton's runner carries no headgear and is a natural closer whose redistribution to the midfield band reflects the crowded hold-up group — the 79-day layoff adds another layer of uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Twilight Glow
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's filly has visor headgear fitted and has been consistent without winning, but her five-run form string includes several midfield finishes on good ground at this sort of trip; her true running style is rear-of-field and she ends up in the midfield section of the map purely because the back of the race is oversubscribed.

runners_data.name: Victory Sound
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 51 and the widest weight concession to receive; a hold-up horse by nature, she is nudged onto the map in midfield simply because there are more hold-up types than positions available at the rear — Gina Mangan claims, which helps, but the rating gap is steep in a seven-runner handicap.

races.paceDynamic: Quick Quasar is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival willing or able to press from the outset, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop across this 7½f trip on good ground at Ffos Las. With six hold-up types behind, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which in theory suits those who can travel prominently — but this field is packed with natural rear-of-field horses, many of whom will be unable to secure their preferred position. Flyta, Twilight Glow, Strong Voice, and Victory Sound are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because there simply is not room at the back for all of them; Quick Quasar and, to a degree, Norfolk Blue and Mayberry Moon are the runners most likely to actually access a forward position. This race shape — a lone, unhurried pace-setter dictating to a field of reluctant closers — strongly favours a horse who can sit close to the tempo, travel without being buried in traffic, and kick from a position of control, making the prominent and tracking profiles the most advantaged.

watchPoints.text: Quick Quasar (Luke Morris) — if she jumps cleanly and is allowed a completely uncontested lead, the true pace of this race rests entirely in her hands; watch whether Morris elects to coast or push on, as that decision shapes every other runner's chance.

Flyta (Billy Loughnane) — a genuine hold-up horse now effectively asked to race in midfield due to the crowded rear; watch how Loughnane positions her early, as any difficulty finding cover could burn her energy before the straight.

Norfolk Blue — 15 days since her most recent run and arguably the strongest recent form in the field, but Taylor Fisher will need to find a clean passage from a hold-up position; watch for any traffic issues on the home turn.

Mayberry Moon — 293 days absent means her fitness is the single biggest unknown in the race; watch for signs of freshness or lethargy in the early stages to gauge whether David Dods's preparation has her ready to fire first time out.
Strong Voice — the 79-day break is worth monitoring in the paddock; if she looks well within herself pre-race this could be a straightforward reappearance run rather than a serious winning attempt.

races.name: Preventapest Handicap

runners_data.name: Grey Soul
runners_data.note: Comes into this in good heart having won two of his last five, with both victories over this exact mile trip — his hold-up style suits a Orchard-led moderate tempo perfectly and Jason Watson has shown he can produce him late; 25 days since last run is straightforward.

runners_data.name: Bold Impact
runners_data.note: Gina Mangan takes the ride for Rod Millman whose T14 strike rate of 1/13 is modest; Bold Impact wants to race prominently but the form string includes a dismal 18th on Good ground and he has not won in some time — capable of placing but inconsistency is a concern.

runners_data.name: Orchard
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who is perfectly placed to dictate here, and Warren Greatrex's yard has decent course knowledge; the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 is a reminder that Orchard's listed position on the map slightly understates his true pace role, and his win record at this trip gives him genuine claims if the tempo suits.

runners_data.name: Pulsar Star
runners_data.note: David Egan takes the mount for the in-form T14 pairing (1/6) and Pulsar Star has placed twice in similar Good-ground conditions — a natural hold-up performer who has placed twice over 7–8f on Good, and 15 days since last run is a fresh enough return; could be the one finishing fastest of all.

runners_data.name: Port Erin
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's runner has a strong winning record at this course (1/8f/GOO in his history) and is a true front-runner by nature — the redistribution to midfield simply reflects that Orchard already has the lead role, and in practice Billy Loughnane may still push him into a prominent position early; his T14 rate of 6/37 is respectable but his recent form reads poorly.

runners_data.name: Port Louis
runners_data.note: Charlie Tucker claims 7lb for Bernard Llewellyn and there is a 49-day gap since last seen — the form string shows repeated modest finishes and the ⚠ fade flag is backed by a history of weakening in the straight; a true hold-up type pushed to midfield on the map, and the combination of long absence and finishing concerns makes this a difficult horse to trust.

races.paceDynamic: Orchard is the one confirmed front runner here and, on Good ground at Ffos Las over a mile, should be able to dictate at a sensible, sustainable tempo without any genuine rival attempting to match strides from the outside. Bold Impact is the most likely horse to press from a prominent position, but with Port Erin also a natural front-runner — redistributed to midfield on the map because the field cannot accommodate all prominent types — Orchard's lead may not be as uncontested as the pace map implies; Port Erin is the more likely of the two displaced prominent horses to push forward and jostle for position in the early stages. The resulting shape should be a single-file, moderate-tempo mile where the pace is honest but not truly strong, with Orchard in control through the long Ffos Las back straight. That dynamic tilts the race emphatically towards hold-up horses with a strong finish, as a steady pace will allow tired horses to drop back and give closers a clear run at a potentially weakening front end — Grey Soul and Pulsar Star are the profile types this shape most rewards.

scenarios.body: If Orchard controls a moderate tempo and is caught late by hold-up horses finishing strongly off the turn.

watchPoints.text: Grey Soul and Pulsar Star — both confirmed hold-up types — are the primary danger if Orchard sets a moderate tempo; watch whether Jason Watson gives Grey Soul a clear passage rounding the home turn as he is the one most likely to deliver a late challenge.

Port Erin's jockey Billy Loughnane may elect to push forward from the gate despite the redistribution — if he does, Orchard's pace advantage is compromised and the early fractions will be sharper than the map implies.

Port Louis's 49-day absence and consistent pattern of fading in the straight make him a horse to keep onside only if he travels ominously well through the early stages — any sign of laboured movement early is a cue to discount him entirely.

Orchard's trainer Warren Greatrex has a T14 record of 0/11 — while Orchard is the likely pace-setter, the yard's recent run of outs is worth noting if assessing whether the horse arrives at peak fitness.

races.name: Plan A Restricted Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Dress For The Occasions Handicap

runners_data.name: Calypso Bloom
runners_data.note: Drops back from 10-11f efforts to 1m4f which is within range, but recent form figures of 8-84 show no consistency and a flagged tendency to fade in the finish on this trip; true hold-up style means she needs others to cut out a strong pace that Beaune is unlikely to provide.

runners_data.name: Beaune
runners_data.note: The race-shaper here — sole confirmed front-runner with T14 support (1/1) and recent wins over 12f on similar ground, though the STYLE_FIT flag notes she can race out of her optimal role; if the pace is hers to control she is the logical anchor of this race.

runners_data.name: Buck Barrow
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle yard is 4/14 in the last fortnight and recent form includes a win over 12f on soft, so the horse clearly stays; a genuine hold-up type pushed into the midfield map because the rear is full, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies — this horse needs more gallop than Beaune is likely to supply.

runners_data.name: Captain Cairney
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from the Muir & Grassick yard who has placed twice on good ground at 10f and won over the same; mapped as a hold-up type but among the most credible to secure a close tracking position in this shape given proven form at the trip and a handy light weight of 128lbs.

runners_data.name: Home Secretary
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's runner was last seen just nine days ago over 12f on good and has a habit of racing wide in hold-up fashion; only one placing in five runs and all recent form at shorter trips suggests this 1m4f on good ground is untested territory — natural closer style further complicated by redistribution.

runners_data.name: Ataturk
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison runner carries a fading-in-finish flag and all three career runs have ended in defeats at 8-10f on soft or good-to-soft; stepping up to 1m4f on good is a significant ask for a lightly raced three-year-old and, as a displaced hold-up type, the pace scenario does him no favours.

runners_data.name: Worlington
runners_data.note: George Boughey has been busy (4/26 T14) and this three-year-old has shown consistent placed form at 8-12f on good ground, including a recent fourth over 12f at a Good track; a true hold-up horse pushed to midfield on the map but with genuine stamina credentials — one of the more credible beneficiaries if the race develops any meaningful late pace.

runners_data.name: Ibn Sirin
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's two-year-old (now three) returns after a 257-day absence having only raced over 8f on good and standard; the absence is a major unknown, the step to 1m4f is untested, and as a displaced hold-up type, there are too many question marks to project a competitive role.

races.paceDynamic: Beaune is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push the pace from the front, she is set to dictate at a sustainable gallop over this 1m4f trip on good ground at Ffos Las. That uncontested lead means the race is likely to be run at a measured, controlled tempo through the early and middle stages, with any serious acceleration coming only in the final two furlongs. This controlled shape fundamentally favours runners who can travel economically close to the pace and produce a sustained finish rather than a sharp sprint — prominent-to-midfield types with proven stamina at this trip are best placed. The field is saturated with genuine hold-up horses: Buck Barrow, Home Secretary, Ataturk, Worlington and Ibn Sirin are all true closers mapped forward on the race shape only because the rear of the field is overcrowded; of the hold-up types, Captain Cairney and Worlington look most likely to actually secure a workable tracking position and get competitive cover, while the rest will likely be shuffled to the back whether they want to be or not.

watchPoints.text: Beaune's early positioning is critical — if Alexandra Egan (claiming 7lbs) goes too hard to establish the lead, the pace ceases to be sustainable and the race shape inverts entirely, eliminating the solo front-runner scenario.

Captain Cairney's jockey Jack Doughty will face a decision from the gate: if he tries to track Beaune at close range he gets the ideal run, but if the hold-up cluster presses forward he may be squeezed into a worse position than his style demands.

Worlington and Buck Barrow are both true closers being asked to race out of their natural position; if they end up on each other's quarters in a compressed midfield it could cause interference and affect the finish for multiple runners.
Ibn Sirin's 257-day layoff makes him an unknown quantity — watch the market move or absence of move in the final 30 minutes as a guide to whether connections believe the horse is fully wound up.

The consistently good going throughout the card at Ffos Las today means no runner gains a surface edge, but Captain Cairney's two placing runs on good ground over 10f are the most directly applicable pieces of form to this specific race shape.
